subjects: Scope and life cycle of data

conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: STRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR9: the DELIMITED phrase may be omitted only immediately preceding INTO; omitted => DELIMITED BY SIZE. BindString back-propagates each DELIMITED phrase over the preceding phraseless run and sets the trailing phraseless run to BySize (`bySize[i] || delims[i] is null`). Because the general format repeats {senders... [DELIMITED ...]}, a phraseless non-final group is indistinguishable from a longer run, so no source can violate the 'only' half; the implied-SIZE half verified by probe gr2.cob C ('S1 DELIMITED BY SPACES "X" DELIMITED SIZE' and the ZERO/SPACE line) and gr1.cob B (`STRING DZ "Q" DELIMITED BY SIZE`). The only covering test (StringUnstringDifferentialTests.String_DelimitedPhraseGovernsItsRun_TrailingRunIsSize) is AssertSameAsLegacy - differential, does not qualify. cite.py --check 14.9.43.3 'The DELIMITED phrase may be omitted only immediately preceding the INTO phrase.' -> OK §14.9.43.3 9). [editions as adjudicated: 2023 text (ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.43); Annex E lists no STRING change 2014->2023; the earlier-edition edge is not derivable in-repo (no 2002/2014 text); whether 85 allowed the omission is not derivable in-repo]
rows.rule-text: The DELIMITED phrase may be omitted only immediately preceding the INTO phrase. If it is omitted, DELIMITED BY SIZE is implied.

rows.subject: STRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR10 is definitional: literal-1/identifier-1 is the sending operand, identifier-3 the receiving operand. The binder binds each stringSendingPhrase operand through the SENDING resolver (StrUnstrOperand -> FieldOperand / LiteralOperand / FigurativeOperand / function-identifier) and identifier-3 and identifier-4 through ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving (the receiving chokepoint - a constant-name or function-identifier INTO is refused there). Consistent with the grammar (stringIntoPhrase : INTO dataReference). No behavior of its own to test. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 text (ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.43); Annex E lists no STRING change 2014->2023; the earlier-edition edge is not derivable in-repo (no 2002/2014 text)]
rows.rule-text: Literal-1 or the data item referenced by identifier-1 is the sending operand. The data item referenced by identifier-3 is the receiving operand.

rows.subject: STRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR10: overlap of identifier-1/-2 with identifier-3/-4, or of identifier-3 with identifier-4, makes the result undefined (cite.py --check 14.9.43.4 'the result of the execution of this statement is undefined' -> OK §14.9.43.4 10); also listed as Annex A undefined item 60). Any behavior conforms; the emitter reads the pointer by value once at initiation and each sender image at its own transfer, writes the receiver image and then the pointer back - deterministic, no crash. No test required for an undefined result. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 text (ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.43); Annex E lists no STRING change 2014->2023; the earlier-edition edge is not derivable in-repo (no 2002/2014 text)]
rows.rule-text: If identifier-1, or identifier-2, occupies the same storage area as identifier-3, or identifier-4, or if identifier-3 and identifier-4 occupy the same storage area, the result of the execution of this statement is undefined, even if they are defined by the same data description entry. (See 14.6.10, Overlapping operands.)

rows.subject: SUPPRESS statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR1 "The SUPPRESS statement may appear only in a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure." (cite.py --check 14.9.45.3 OK). BindSuppress rejects with COBOLNET1581 when ctx.Enclosing.Declarative?.ReportGroup is null. Probes: sr1a.cob (SUPPRESS in nondeclarative MAIN) -> COBOLNET1581; sr1b.cob (SUPPRESS in a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR declarative) -> COBOLNET1581; sr1c.cob (SUPPRESS in a nondeclarative paragraph PERFORMed from the BEFORE REPORTING declarative; the rule is lexical 'appear') -> COBOLNET1581. No spec-derived negative test for COBOLNET1581 found in tests/ -> test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2014, 2023 (not an Annex E 2014->2023 addition, so present in 2014); 85/2002 availability not derivable from the 2023 text (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 130d, RW accepted at every edition)]
rows.rule-text: The SUPPRESS statement may appear only in a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure.

rows.subject: SUPPRESS statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR3 a-e (cite.py --check 14.9.45.4 3) d) and 3) e) OK). Every presentation path returns right after RunBeforeReporting reports suppression, before page-fit/AdvancePage, PresentLine (LINE-COUNTER) and ApplyNextGroup; PresentBody keeps only EndOfGroupSumReset. Control-break detection/processing in GenerateCore precedes PresentBody(detail), so (e) holds. Probes gr3.cob/gr3b.cob (PAGE LIMIT 12, FIRST DETAIL 2, LAST DETAIL 7, FOOTING 9, DE NEXT GROUP PLUS 1, SOURCE LINE-COUNTER): suppressed details leave LINE-COUNTER unchanged (4->4, 6->6, 8->8), no NEXT GROUP applied; a suppressed detail at LINE-COUNTER 8 (fit would fail) causes no page advance (PAGE-COUNTER stays 1, CF then prints at 9); a suppressed detail that triggers a control break still prints CF-1 and CH-2 on the next page. conformance:2023/rw_suppress covers only (a) -> test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 2014, 2023 (not an Annex E 2014->2023 addition, so present in 2014); 85/2002 availability not derivable from the 2023 text (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 130d, RW accepted at every edition)]
rows.rule-text: When the SUPPRESS statement is executed, the following report group functions are inhibited: a) The printing of the print lines of the report group. b) Any page advance associated with the report group. c) The processing of any NEXT GROUP clause in the report group. d) Any changes to LINE-COUNTER associated with the report group. e) If the associated report group is a detail, the SUPPRESS statement does not affect the sensing for control breaks or the subsequent control break processing.

rows.subject: Scope and life cycle of data
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "both programs may refer to data possessing the global attribute either in the containing program or in any program that directly or indirectly contains the containing program." (cite.py --check 8.6.7: OK §8.6.7 2)). Code: BinderDriver.BindUnitData walks every ancestor (nearest container first, local names shadow) and adds anc.Data.GlobalBridgesOf(g, outer) ref-bridges over the CONTAINER INSTANCE's fields, so containee and container address one storage. Probe (--std 85 and --std 2023): GOUTER{G1 GLOBAL, G1T GLOBAL table, L1 non-global} > GMID{G2 GLOBAL} > GIN; GIN adds to G1 (indirect container), G2 (direct container), stores G1E(2): output MID G1=102 G2=025 / OUTER G1=102 G1E2=ZZ L1=007 / MID G1=203 G2=030 / OUTER G1=203 -- both halves (direct and indirect) share storage, and state persists across calls. Negative edge: GIN referencing non-global L1 -> COBOLNET1639 undefined (correct). Test-ref left empty: conformance:2002/pb1009_global_linkage_formal, 2023/pb163_global_local_storage and 2002/pb1019 cover only the DIRECT-container half; no spec-derived conformance test references a GLOBAL item of an INDIRECTLY containing program (test-needed for that half). [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (GLOBAL/nested programs are in every edition)]
rows.rule-text: If a program is contained within another program, both programs may refer to data possessing the global attribute either in the containing program or in any program that directly or indirectly contains the containing program.

rows.subject: Scope of statements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: the explicit terminator also terminates 'any unterminated statements that appear between that statement-name and the explicit scope terminator' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.2 -> OK §14.5.3.2 2)). Mechanism: statementBlock : statement+ stops at any END_x token that cannot start a statement; each intervening rule's own END_y? is absent, so it closes implicitly and control returns up the rule stack to the rule owning END_x. Probes: IF ... ADD ON SIZE ERROR ... END-IF closes the ADD (sc1 T3 -> 'T3 SE','T3 AFTER-IF'); ADD ON SIZE ERROR IF ... END-ADD closes the IF (sc1 T4); PERFORM ... IF ... END-PERFORM (sc4 U1); EVALUATE WHEN IF ... END-EVALUATE (sc4 U2); SEARCH WHEN IF ... END-SEARCH (sc4 U7) - all as the rule requires, at 85 and 2023. (U1/U2/U7 place an undelimited conditional where a format writes imperative-statement; that acceptance is PB351's open under-reject, not this row.) No existing spec-derived test crosses an intervening unterminated statement: test-needed. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]
rows.rule-text: any unterminated statements that appear between that statement-name and the explicit scope terminator.

rows.subject: Scope of statements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: a single imperative statement not contained in another is terminated by 'a) any element that follows the exhaustion of the statement's syntax, or b) the next-encountered statement-name, or c) a separator period' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 1) a)). Mechanism: sentence : statement+ DOT, each statement rule consumes exactly its own syntax, so the next statement keyword (b), the DOT (c), or a following element such as ELSE (a) ends it. Probes: 'DISPLAY "T8 A" DISPLAY "T8 B" MOVE 1 TO A DISPLAY A.' -> three separate statements (sc1 T8); every sentence in sc1/sc4 ends at its period. Reserved statement names cannot be absorbed as operands (§8.9 reservation), so no adversarial operand/statement-name collision exists. No spec-derived test targets this rule specifically: test-needed. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]
rows.rule-text: for a single imperative statement not contained within another statement, by a) any element that follows the exhaustion of the statement's syntax, or b) the next-encountered statement-name, or c) a separator period.

rows.subject: Scope of statements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'for a conditional statement not contained within another statement, by a separator period' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 3)). Mechanism: a phrase's statementBlock is statement+ and only DOT (or a phrase/terminator token) ends it, so every following statement up to the period belongs to the conditional phrase. Probes: 'IF FLG = 2 DISPLAY "U4 WRONG1" DISPLAY "U4 WRONG2".' prints neither (sc4 U4); 'ADD 1 TO A ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY "U5 SE" DISPLAY "U5 SE2".' runs both only on size error (sc4 U5); top-level ADD with nested phrases runs to its period (sc1 T2). The golden's S1 pins it for IF (both IFs terminated by the sentence's period). probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref EMPTY (test-needed) — The implementation conforms (sc4 U4/U5, refuter R2/R3/R8 all end at the period), but the cited golden does NOT decide this rule: in S1 the outer IF is TRUE and the inner else-arm executes, so had the period failed to end the outer (or inner) IF every later statement would fall inside an executed arm and the output would be IDENTICAL. The golden header itself says each shape is chosen so candidate readings differ, and that holds only for ELSE/END-IF matching (14.9.19.3 SR2), not for period termination. A non-discriminating golden must not close the row. A deciding test needs e.g. IF false DISPLAY "a". DISPLAY "b". (b must print). [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]
rows.rule-text: for a conditional statement not contained within another statement, by a separator period.

rows.subject: Scope of statements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: a contained conditional statement is terminated by the termination or next phrase of a containing statement; 'Any phrase encountered is the next phrase of the most-recently preceding unterminated statement with which that phrase may be syntactically associated. If all permitted occurrences of a phrase have already been specified for a given statement, a subsequent occurrence of that phrase is not syntactically associated with that statement' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 4)). Mechanism: each conditional-phrase group allows each phrase at most once (e.g. arithmeticOnSizeError, readAtEnd, ifStatement's single ELSE), and ANTLR's greedy optional attaches a phrase to the innermost open rule that can still take it, returning outward otherwise - the rule's association order. Probes: nested IFs, second ELSE goes to the outer IF (sc1 T6 'T6 OUTER-ELSE', T6B 'T6B INNER-ELSE'); END-IF-terminated inner IF lets ELSE go outer (sc1 T7); ADD conditional inside IF ended by ELSE (sc1 T9); SEARCH inside IF ended by ELSE, both WHENs to SEARCH (sc4 U6 'U6 FOUND'); exhausted inner NOT ON SIZE ERROR passes the second NOT to the outer ADD (sc1 T1/T2). The golden's S1/S3 pin association and the 'already matched with an ELSE' exhaustion for IF. Reach note: §14.5.1 makes a conditional statement imperative only when delimited, and every Table-12 conditional phrase and EVALUATE/PERFORM body is written imperative-statement-n, so in a CONFORMING program the only containing statement a conditional can sit in unterminated is IF (§14.9.19.2 statement-1/-2), whose only later phrase is ELSE. The grammar over-admits phrase repetition/merging elsewhere (SEARCH ALL WHEN+ - PB446; READ Format 1 AT END with Format 2 INVALID KEY on one statement; WRITE EOP with INVALID KEY; CALL 'NOT ON OVERFLOW'), which could steal a phrase from an outer statement - but only in programs already non-conforming under PB351 (undelimited conditional in an imperative position). Those rows are owned by PB351/PB446; no separate scope defect. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref EMPTY (test-needed) — Implementation conforms: adjudicator sc1 T6 (IF IF ELSE ELSE, second ELSE to outer), refuter R2 (ELSE terminates a contained undelimited EVALUATE, both truth values), R3 (ELSE terminates contained READ AT END/NOT AT END), R8, E5 (third ELSE with both IFs exhausted rejected COBOL0307). But the golden does not pin the rule load-bearing branches: branch b) "next phrase of any containing statement" terminating a contained CONDITIONAL, and the exhaustion sentence, are never reached - in S2/S3/S4 every inner IF is END-IF terminated before the ELSE (so S3 is decided by the END-IF, not by the already-matched-ELSE exhaustion the adjudicator credits it with), and in S1 the inner IF is ended by the period. Only the association sentence (S1 dangling ELSE) is pinned. A deciding test: IF T IF F DISPLAY 1 ELSE DISPLAY 2 ELSE DISPLAY 3. with no END-IF (expect 2), plus IF F IF .. ELSE .. ELSE DISPLAY 3. (expect 3). [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]
rows.rule-text: for a conditional statement contained within another statement, by a) the termination of any containing statement, or b) the next phrase of any containing statement. Any phrase encountered is the next phrase of the most-recently preceding unterminated statement with which that phrase may be syntactically associated. If all permitted occurrences of a phrase have already been specified for a given statement, a subsequent occurrence of that phrase is not syntactically associated with that statement. An unterminated statement is any statement that has begun but has not yet been either explicitly or implicitly terminated. A contained statement is also referred to as a nested statement.

rows.subject: Simple boolean condition
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'Boolean-expression-1 shall reference only boolean items of length 1.' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.3.3 OK). BoolExprAllLengthOne walks every leaf; a violation is COBOLNET1511. Probed n1.cob: IF B8 (PIC 1(8)), NOT B8, B8 B-AND B8, BW B-AND B8, B8(1:2), G2 (GROUP-USAGE BIT of 2 bits -- §13.18.29.4 GR1b PICTURE 1(m), cite.py --check OK), BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(1,2), B-NOT B8, PERFORM UNTIL B8 all -> COBOLNET1511; EVALUATE TRUE WHEN B8 -> COBOLNET1634 (Table 15). Legal side: every length-1 form in p1.cob accepted; a run-time-length ref-mod (B(1:N)) fails open, correct for a syntax rule (pb589_bool_refmod_width.cob covers that acceptance). Note (not a divergence): the code also refuses a boolean LITERAL longer than 1 (`IF B"10"`, `IF BW B-OR B"10"`); the SR's words name only items, but such an expression's result is not 1 or 0, so GR1 assigns it no truth value -- refusing it is the only reading under which the condition is defined. Shift with a long operand (`IF B8 B-SHIFT-L 1`) is refused, but by the wrong diagnostic (COBOLNET2318, the FMT finding's HasBoolOp mechanism). No spec-derived NEGATIVE test exists for the procedure-division SR1 refusal (CompileTimeBooleanCceTests covers the >>IF CCE path only) -- test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85 -- boolean data/operators arrive at 2002; the 2023 Annex E.2 item 3 adds ONLY the B-SHIFT-* operators at 2023, so a shift-form boolean-expression-1 is 2023-only)]
rows.rule-text: Boolean-expression-1 shall reference only boolean items of length 1.
